name.text: Types of Functions — identifying degree from a disguised expression

questiontext.text:
Consider the function, written in an unexpanded form:

\[ y = {@displayexpr@}. \]

Once fully expanded, what type of function is this?

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]

generalfeedback.text:
The type of a polynomial function is decided by its degree, the highest power of \(x\) that remains after the expression is fully expanded and like terms are collected: degree 1 is linear, degree 2 is quadratic and degree 3 is cubic.

Expanding fully: \[ {@displayexpr@} = {@degexpr@}. \]

[[if test="is(scenario=0)"]]

Both squares contain \(x^2\), and the two \(x^2\) terms cancel when one square is subtracted from the other.

[[elif test="is(scenario=1)"]]

Both cubes contain \(x^3\), and the two \(x^3\) terms cancel when one cube is subtracted from the other.

[[else]]

The \(x^2\) terms cancel, but the \(x^3\) term from the product remains.

[[/if]]

The degree is \({@deg@}\), so this is a {@ftype_opt@} function. Do not judge the type from how the expression looks before expanding: terms can cancel and lower the degree.

questiondescription.text: Grade 11 Functions 16.5 (Types of Functions). Classifies a function by degree after full expansion; the unexpanded form is deliberately deceptive (a difference of two squares or two cubes whose leading terms cancel, or a product with a cancelling x^2 term) so that judging by appearance alone leads to the wrong answer.

node.description: Correct type after expanding (dropdown: no diagnostic)

falsefeedback.text: Expand the expression fully and collect like terms first. Then look at the highest power of \(x\) that remains: some terms may cancel.

qtest.description: Wrong type guessed from unexpanded form
